title: Asking for and Giving Directions
summary: In this lesson, you will learn how to ask where places are in a city. You will also learn how to tell people the way.

sections.p: When you are in a new city and want to find a place, you need to ask for help. A polite way to start is by saying 'Excuse me'. Then, you can ask where a specific place is. We use the verb 'is' for one place. For example, you can ask about a bank, a hotel, or a station. People will be happy to help you if you are polite.

ex.en: Excuse me, where is the train station?
ex.mean: Asking politely to find the station.

ex.en: Excuse me, is there a bank near here?
ex.mean: Asking if a bank is close to your location.
A simple way to ask for the shop.

sections.p: When someone asks you for help, you need to give them clear instructions. You can tell them to go straight, turn left, or turn right. These three simple phrases are very important. You can also use words like 'next to' or 'opposite' to show where a building is.

To ask for directions, you need to know the names of common places in a city. A city has many useful buildings and areas. Knowing these words helps you understand the answers people give you. For example, you might need a hospital, a park, or a cafe.

ex.en: The hotel is next to the park.
ex.mean: The hotel and park are side by side.

ex.en: The cafe is opposite the museum.
ex.mean: The cafe is on the other side of the street from the museum.

words.mean: polite way to start talking to a stranger

tip: Use your hands when you point left or right to help people understand you better. Always start with a smile and 'Excuse me'.

quiz.ask: Choose the correct phrase to start asking a question.
Choose the correct direction for walking forward.
Choose the correct word for changing direction to the side of your writing hand.
Choose the correct preposition when a place is across the street.
Choose the correct verb to ask about one place.
Choose the correct phrase when a place is beside another.
quiz.en: The bank is ___ the post office.
